A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OneStop reading-goal decoding study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable matching despite extensive restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, ensemble, ROC/AUC and mixed-effects analysis results on 19,438 OneStop trials.

after.justification: v2 reports original classification and analysis results, including additional vision-model comparisons and predictions from partial reading sequences.

M1.justification: v2 introduces a scanpath-image modeling branch using ViT and ConvNeXt V2, encoding fixation duration, sequence progression and saccade categories visually. The proposed Logistic Ensemble expands from ten to twelve model-probability inputs. These extend the modeling pipeline; the original individual architectures retain their described procedures.

E1.justification: The OneStop texts, participants and two reading goals remain unchanged. v2 adds prediction during unfinished readings using initial scanpath segments, extending coverage beyond completed readings. The auxiliary question-difficulty source also changes from the external Prolific QA experiment to training data.

E2.justification: Table 1 and v2's validation Table 4 add ViT and ConvNeXt V2 as evaluated scanpath-image comparators. The original ten predictors, Reading Time baseline and Majority Class baseline remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation using the first 1%, 5%, 10%, 25% and 50% of fixations. Its error-analysis equation replaces binary correctness with correct-label probability, and question difficulty is estimated from training data instead of Prolific QA responses. The stated cross-validation design and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6 and Table 2 add a substantial analysis of how early accurate decoding becomes possible. The existing ten-feature error analysis is revised around prediction confidence, with changed coefficients and findings. Agreement analyses also incorporate the vision models; the feature descriptions themselves largely move to Appendix F.

E5.justification: v2 adds 95% confidence intervals to test and partial-scanpath accuracies, interval estimates to validation results, and significance comparisons against the best individual model. v1 already reported mixed-effects significance tests and AUC variability. Ten cross-validation splits and the error analysis's Bonferroni correction are retained; no increased run count is stated.

E6.justification: Reported All test accuracy changes from 68.5% to 90.3% for RoBERTa-Eye-F and from 66.1% to 89.3% for PostFusion-Eye. RoBERTa-Eye-F becomes the best individual model in every regime. New results include 77.6% accuracy from the first 5% of fixations. Ensemble, validation, coefficient and agreement results also change substantially, while v1 Figure 6's ROC/AUC values remain in v2 Figure 8.

T1.justification: The displayed mixed-effects specification changes its response from is_correct in v1 Section 6 to P(correct) in v2 Section 7, retaining the predictors and random-effects structure. This changes the mathematical specification, although v2's separate references to logits leave the response scale ambiguous. The task definition remains unchanged, with no added theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Beyond v1's successful decoding and ensemble contributions, v2 makes early, real-time prediction a central claim. Its abstract, introduction and conclusion emphasize transformer-based fixation representations combined with text, and present mixed-effects modeling of model logits as a new general method for performance analysis.

C2.justification: v2 interprets architecture, fixation-level representation and textual input as key to success, and develops online application implications. It adds explicit newswire and 3–10-line paragraph limitations. Its revised generalization discussion incorrectly says weaker models favor New Participant, whereas Table 1 mostly shows higher New Item accuracy, weakening that interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix A adds scanpath-rendering details and exact vision checkpoint identifiers. Most training and hardware information is retained. The code-access pointer changes to an anonymous repository, while v1's explicit validation-set ensemble-fitting procedure and promised public data release are no longer stated.

R1.justification: v2 adds vision and image-gaze references, including Bhattacharya et al., Dosovitskiy et al. and Woo et al., plus reading-task and text-property prediction literature and the OneStop dataset paper. Some corpus and ensemble-survey citations disappear. Positioning against the closest information-seeking and ZuCo studies remains broadly intact.

P1.justification: Model descriptions become short main-text bullets with detailed versions in Appendix A; feature motivations move to Appendix F, and ensemble methodology moves from Results to Modeling. The abstract, introduction and discussion are extensively revised. A separate Limitations section is introduced and the Reproducibility Statement is removed.

P2.justification: The main text switches to two columns. Accuracy tables are rebuilt with intervals, additional comparators and ensemble rows; Table 2 and scanpath/architecture Figures 4–6 are added. The ensemble bar chart disappears, coefficient and agreement displays are revised, and retained task, split, dataset-example and ROC figures are relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful comparator coverage, early-prediction evidence, uncertainty reporting and architecture diagrams. However, central reporting becomes inconsistent: RoBERTa-Eye-F's New Participant accuracy changes from 63.1% to 90.9%, while Figure 8 retains v1's AUROC of 0.69 without explanation. The revised error analysis also alternates between logits, probability and binary correctness. These unresolved issues affect central contributions and prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
